purpose: Nafarelin is used to treat endometriosis, a painful condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus. It is also used in children to treat central precocious puberty, which means puberty that starts too early. By reducing certain hormone levels, it helps relieve pain and slow abnormal tissue growth or early puberty.
how_it_works: Your body normally uses a hormone signal to tell your ovaries or testes to make sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone. Nafarelin works by flooding that signal so much that your body eventually stops responding to it. This causes hormone levels to drop significantly, which reduces the growth of endometriosis tissue or slows down early puberty in children.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes, headaches, mood changes, decreased sex drive, vaginal dryness, acne, muscle aches, nasal irritation where the spray is used, and irregular or stopped periods are common. These effects happen because the medication lowers your estrogen levels.
warnings: This medication can cause a temporary loss of bone density, so long-term use should be monitored carefully. It should NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm the unborn baby — use reliable non-hormonal birth control. Tell your doctor about any history of osteoporosis or bone loss. If you notice depression or serious mood changes, contact your doctor right away. Do not use nasal decongestant sprays within 30 minutes of using this medication.
typical_dosing: For endometriosis, the usual dose is one spray (200 mcg) into one nostril in the morning and one spray into the other nostril in the evening — that is two sprays per day. Treatment usually lasts up to 6 months. For children with early puberty, dosing is higher and determined by the doctor based on the child's weight and response.
